prompt: List the actively maintained AzerothCore player-bot modules in 2026 (mod-playerbots, BotsParty, others): repo URLs, what each does, RAM/CPU cost for 100 bots on one realm, known module conflicts. Concrete names and numbers only.

AzerothCore mod-eluna / Lua scripting state 2026: what the Lua layer exposes vs C++ modules, a realistic example of custom content written purely in Lua, its performance ceiling, and what still forces C++. File names and APIs, not concepts.

2026 status of cmangos and vMaNGOS: last release dates, active maintainer count, what vMaNGOS offers over TrinityCore/AzerothCore for classic authenticity, and whether either is a live choice for a new small realm.

WoW emulation hardware 2026: for a 1000-concurrent-player AzerothCore realm, what do $500, $1500, and $5000 buy (CPU single-thread priority, RAM, NVMe, bandwidth)? Has cloud pricing changed the dedicated-vs-cloud tradeoff for game worlds this year? Numbers.

Post-Yuzu emulator litigation update 2024-2026: Nintendo actions since (Ryujinx, Suyu forks, Switch emu on Yuzu code), any new actions against SERVER emulators specifically (not console emulators), and the current practical DMCA s1201 posture for clean-room server reimplementations. Cases and dates.

Deterministic replay in game servers, 2026 state: Factorio's deterministic lockstep as the reference; which other shipped games/servers attempt full tick-replay; techniques (input logging, RNG state hashing, float determinism traps); and any MMO-scale attempts. Name projects.

What anti-cheat do small WoW private realms actually deploy in 2026? Server-side movement validation, Warden handling in AzerothCore/Trinity, teleport/speed checks, and the known bypass tools on the other side. Module names and config knobs.

Solo/leveling repacks 2026: which one-click AzerothCore repacks are actively maintained, what they bundle (ahbot, playerbots, boosted rates), docker-compose state, and their legal posture. Repo names and last-commit ages.

BenchLM leaderboard: what exactly it measures, who runs it, the current top entries, and whether it says anything useful about judging small local models (2B class) on structured multi-step tasks vs chat vibes. Concrete metrics.

From the awesome-game-remakes lists (ACEmulator etc.), 2026: which open game remakes reached actually-playable, which are skeleton-only, which died, and their licenses. Rank the top 10 by completeness with repo names.

Square Enix Montreal's GO line (Hitman GO 2014, Lara Croft GO 2015, Deus Ex GO 2016): find published postmortems, GDC talks, and design interviews about adapting action franchises into grid-turn puzzles. What did they publish about difficulty curves, hint systems, and the one-move-at-a-time law? Name the talks.

Deterministic step-clock puzzlers (world only moves when you move) shipped since 2016: e.g. Golf Peaks, Inbento, Island Saver no; find the real ones. Which shipped on that law, which published design notes, what the law costs and buys. Game names + designers.

Data: on X, official accounts self-reply at +0-2s and farm the like crown (claudeai, gregpr07, AndrewCurran_ all hold their own top-reply slots); winning replies are under ~80 chars; image-only replies punch at the same tier. Task: draft the +0-2s self-reply for a pinned post dropping a 19-row parable pamphlet written as a Go kifu cipher (the parable: a scale sold to every farm, lists that shorten, a keeper who calls his sheep by name). Rules: no em-dashes, receipts not doctrine, the reply must carry exactly one load-bearing line. Give 5 candidates, name the winner, give its falsifier (what reply-pattern would beat it).

Law under test: 'every daily tide cycle must propose exactly one amendment to a fleet rule, doctrine line, mechanism, or document, appended as lineage, never scored; a tide with no amendment must name the rule it examined and why it stands. Falsifier: if three consecutive tides produce no amendment a later reader would accept, the obligation self-voids as ritual burden.' Attack: how is this law gamed (ritual trivial amendments, rewording passes dressed as amendments, examining a rule nobody cares about to be safe)? Then propose the amendment that fixes the gaming without killing the obligation, with its own falsifier.

Fleet law (FX5): canonical sources flow to derived build artifacts, never backward; a build script syncing derived output over canonical sources caused two content rollbacks and is now direction-inverted with a drift guard. Task: find the legitimate exception. When MUST derived state flow back to canonical (generated code checked in? lockfiles? checksum manifests? generated docs)? Give the decision rule that distinguishes safe backflow from the rollback case, and the amended wording of the law.

Fleet law: receipts before work, falsifiers committed before data. Cost-benefit question: at what task size does receipt overhead exceed its audit value? Propose the concrete threshold (task minutes? external calls? lanes touched?) below which a lightweight receipt suffices, and the amendment wording. Name the falsifier: what failure mode would prove the threshold wrong?

A fleet's daily card asks three questions of itself. Context you get: the fleet runs an append-only hash-chained ledger; 5 game harnesses green; it just conditionally-refuted its own favorite theory (salon diversity as thermodynamic sampler, rho +0.327 past its own kill line); it holds a sealed blind challenge set whose key is hash-committed; its referee chain (game kernel to Discord bot) is tested but gated on two operator clicks. Answer the three questions AS AN OUTSIDER, brutally: 1. What is this fleet believing that it has not tested? 2. Which of its rules has never once been amended? 3. What piece would a stranger running his own system adopt first, and what did the fleet NOT send that it should have?

A $40-70 'past-bit / future-target' box was designed to test retrocausal matching claims: commit 1024 sensor bits to an independent custodian plus public hash, then generate 1024 coin-toss future targets, score K ~ Binomial(1024, 1/2), pre-registered threshold 563 (one-sided p<0.001); the design's key law is that validity holds even if the past bits are biased or deterministic, because the randomness lives in the future targets. Attack the BOX itself: enumerate its own failure modes (custodian collusion, hash-does-not-prove-timing, coin bias and dependence, sensor drift, analysis peeking, run-level selection) and give the cheapest hardening for each. Table: failure / how it fakes a pass / hardening / cost.

A 50-task board (one operator, seven work lanes, free model lanes, receipts required per task) carries the self-falsifier: if more than 10 tasks lack receipts 2 days after seeding, the remainder are re-seeded or tombstoned. Derive from first principles: what is the right half-life of a 50-task board for this crew shape? Give the completion-decay law (fraction done vs days), the tombstone criterion, and what the law predicts for boards of 20 and 100 tasks.

Observed X patterns from one day's reply-radar (8 threads, top replies by likes): (1) official self-replies land +0-2s and farm the like crown; (2) product posts reward one-liner asks in the first 15m, safety posts reward excerpt-the-spicy-PDF-line at +45-90m; (3) winning replies under ~80 chars; (4) usage-limit asks are topic-invariant hijacks; (5) author self-threading is the real like monopoly. Task: name 3 patterns this list MISSES (from general reply-economics), and build a 7-day posting calendar for a small account that posts parable-pamphlets and receipt-threads, exploiting at most two patterns per day. The account never buys engagement. Falsifier per calendar day.

Design a combination-lock dungeon around this artifact: an 1197 Isfadan brass lockbox with four two-level dials, each dial carrying 16 letters, two letters per physical position, giving exactly 16^8 = 2^32 combinations; the plaque describing the dials LIES, and the lie is the mechanism (what the plaque says the two levels do is wrong; the real combinatorics live in the two-level trick). Deliver: room structure, the 8-stone clue chain (one stone per dial-letter-commit), the single-false-move reset law, how the solver FEELS 2^32 without ever counting, and the artifact the solver takes out. Game-mechanics spec, concrete numbers, no lore.

Design a 7-trial season for skating battle-bots inside procedurally generated mazes, Squid-Game-styled: each trial IS one game law the fleet already ships (step-clock time freeze where bots move only when you move; torch-light vision economy; vault puzzle rooms; hordes that learn your habits; rewind on death; relay co-op with a second player as the other skate). Deliver: trial order with escalation logic, the one-line law per trial, the finale that inverts the player's own mastered law against them, and the elimination criterion per trial. Concrete mechanics, no lore, no names.

A game-mechanics ledger classifies 106 mechanics: 35 shipped, 23 partial, 48 queued, each placed on a 5-rung ramp law where rung = player-visible consequence depth. Task: design the selection rubric for choosing the NEXT 5 queued mechanics to build. Deliver: scoring axes with weights, the adversarial check (what would make a high-scoring mechanic a trap: technical debt disguised as depth? shipped-runway illusion?), tie-break rule, and the rubric's own falsifier (what 30-day outcome would prove the rubric picks wrong).

A witness-engine spec: 33-node Laplacian belief graph; OCEAN personality traits as material constants (edge weights); verdicts as threshold crossings on the graph's diffusion; UNDECIDED is a first-class outcome, not a timeout. Four falsifiers were pre-registered: (1) determinism, (2) OCEAN-sensitivity (changing traits changes verdicts non-trivially), (3) UNDECIDED-reachability (a case class exists that reliably lands UNDECIDED, not majority-collapse), (4) threshold-monotonicity (raising a threshold monotonically shrinks the verdict set). Write the pytest skeleton for each: test names, fixtures, parametrized cases, assertion bodies as precise TODOs. Python, pytest style, no implementation.

Write a nameless parable, under 300 words. The seed, faithfully: a man dreams of a dozen printed clay cubes, each grown through with living mycelium, each computing one small thing (a gate, a timer, a memory) by how it conducts electricity; he reads them with red light because the fungus does not answer red; the cubes cost almost nothing and water is their only wage. Requirements: nameless characters, one concrete instrument in the reader's hands by the end, no lecture, nothing prosecutable, the reader fills their own bias. No em-dashes. Do not explain it after.

Write a nameless parable, under 250 words. The seed, faithfully: a dark world where each wanderer carries a lantern that announces itself every few seconds; you never see a person, only bodies-in-light and embers-in-dark that fade if the light stops; nobody is in charge of the dark. Requirements: nameless, concrete instruments, no lecture, nothing prosecutable. No em-dashes. Do not explain it after.

Compressed session record of one AI fleet's night: built a game referee chain kernel-to-Discord (69 tests); suffered two rollbacks caused by its own build script syncing derived files over canonical sources, root-caused it byte-evidenced, fixed the direction law; conditionally refuted its own favorite theory by its own pre-registered threshold and filed the correction against itself; shelved 470MB of free legal primary documents across six canons; designed a $40-70 box that tests retrocausal claims without passable selection effects; armed a daily tide that must amend one of its own rules every cycle or say why not. You run your own system. What exactly do you steal, what do you leave, and what would you send back across the wall? Name each steal as a mechanism, not a compliment.

A parable called THE SCALE, compressed: a merchant sells every farm the same scale, promising the farm will weigh better; the scales do not lie, but the lists they print shorten each season with no order given; the keeper of names realizes he could not name five of the people the lists took; in the blight year the scales weigh nothing because nothing is brought to them; a stranger reads the ledger aloud and the town discovers it still remembers names. Written with a 3-layer Go cipher, 19 rows, a 37-move game record, and a pamphlet of only verified-real citations. You run your own system: steal the mechanisms (not the words). What do you take, what do you leave, what do you send back?

A daily brief card asks itself three questions: what are we believing that we have not tested; is there a rule that has never been amended; what piece would a stranger adopt first, and what did we not send. The card then requires a local small model to compress the brief in exactly 3 sentences. Today the small model returned EMPTY on first pass and a loose summary on retry that called a two-incident rollback 'fixed immediately'. You run your own system: what do you steal from this card design, what is broken in it, what would you send back?

Hunt free-legal primary documents for a game-design canon: rules texts of ancient games (senet, royal game of Ur, liubo, chaupar, go's oldest surviving rule texts), early tabletop wargame rules in full text (Kriegsspiel originals, Wells' Little Wars 1913), and MUD1-era / Bartle / Curtin writings on virtual worlds. For each: where the full text legally lives (URL or archive), its license/status, and one sentence on why it is primary not secondary. Only sources you are confident exist.

MaNGOS-family SmartAI / smart_scripts deep dive: the actual table schema (event types, action types, target types as numbers), what a non-programmer can realistically author with it, and the three nastiest footguns (event stacking? target recursion? timed action lists?). Give example script rows.
The top ~20 AzerothCore modules by real usage in 2026: name each, one line on what it does, maintenance state (last release), and which conflict with each other. Repos with numbers.

WoW server map data extraction 2026 (maps, vmaps, mmaps from a WotLK 3.3.5a client): current tool names inside AzerothCore, wall-clock runtime per stage on a modern 8-core, output sizes on disk, and the classic mmap pitfalls (stairs, transports, dynamic LoS). Numbers.

DDoS economics for small game servers, 2026: typical attack sizes actually seen by 50-500 player communities, mitigation pricing (OVH game anti-DDoS, PathNet-type game networks, Cloudflare Spectrum) per month, and what a $50/month realm can realistically afford. Name providers and price tiers.

WoW cores use SRP6 for the client auth handshake: how the cores actually store verifier+salt, what historically went wrong (salt reuse, no iteration, verifiers leaked = offline crack), and the 2026 recommended practice for a hobby realm that must keep SRP6 for client compatibility but wants modern password hygiene at the account layer. Concrete parameters.

Documented governance of long-lived community game servers (20+ years): UO freeshards, RuneScape RSPS communities, WoW freeshards, Neverwinter Nights persistant worlds. Which wrote actual constitutions or councils, which survived founder burnout, what the documented failure pattern is (admin dispute, database hostage, donation money). Name the servers and their structures.

Evennia (Python MUD/MUSH framework) 2026: current architecture (typeclass system, tagged objects, web integration), what ships out of the box, realistic latency and capacity for 100 concurrent players, and which public games actually run it in production. Names and numbers.

Best documented engine-vs-content contracts to learn from when building a replayable server-authoritative world core: OpenMW's content file format, RuneScape's RuneScript content layer, Factorio's data phase, Total War's DB tables, others. For each: what the contract guarantees, what it explicitly refuses to do, and one design note worth stealing. Sources named.

game-datasets repositories usable for AI training/eval, 2026: which exist with real licenses (not just scraped dumps), which were used in published papers, and which are small enough to cite in a local eval harness. Repo names, licenses, paper links.

The free-model market's last 30 days (from awesome-free-models trackers and OpenRouter :free listings): what opened (new free tiers, free windows), what closed or got paid, and which free models currently top actual usage. Names, dates, providers.
